tour.name: Manaus Private Amazon Day Tour: the Meeting of the Waters, Pink Dolphins & the Teatro Amazonas
tour.subtitle: A private day on the Amazon with a licensed guide and boat: the Teatro Amazonas of the rubber boom, the Meeting of the Waters where the black Rio Negro and the sandy Solimões flow side by side, giant water lilies, a canoe through the flooded forest, and pink river dolphins.

tour.overview:
Manaus lies in the heart of the Amazon, on the Rio Negro just above its junction with the Solimões. At the end of the 19th century, the rubber boom made it one of the richest cities in the world, with electric trams and a pink opera house, the Teatro Amazonas, built with materials shipped from Europe and opened in 1896. Just downstream, the dark, acidic waters of the Rio Negro meet the warmer, faster, sandy waters of the Solimões, and the two flow side by side for several kilometres without mixing before forming the Amazon proper.

This private day takes you on the rivers with a licensed guide and a boat, from the opera house to the Meeting of the Waters, the flooded forest, the giant water lilies and the pink river dolphins.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Manaus
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, private boat, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Teatro Amazonas.
• The Adolpho Lisboa market.
• The Meeting of the Waters.
• The Janauari lake and its water lilies.
• Pink river dolphins.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private boat lets you stop when wildlife appears and reach quieter channels than the big tour boats.

WHO IT SUITS
Nature lovers, families and anyone with a day in Manaus before or after a jungle lodge.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To experience the rainforest more deeply, ask us for a 3- or 4-day stay at a jungle lodge.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The water level varies by up to 10 metres between the high-water season (May to July), when canoes glide through the treetops, and the low-water season (October to November), when beaches appear.

days.name: The Teatro Amazonas, the Meeting of the Waters, the flooded forest and the pink dolphins
days.description:
What to expect: the city of the rubber boom and the great rivers, with a licensed guide, private boat, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:00. You start at the Teatro Amazonas, its dome covered in 36,000 glazed tiles in the colours of the Brazilian flag. Inside, you see the auditorium with its painted ceiling of the Eiffel Tower seen from below, and the ballroom with a floor of thousands of pieces of Amazon wood. You then visit the Adolpho Lisboa market, an iron hall modelled on Les Halles in Paris, with its stalls of giant pirarucu fish, guaraná and tropical fruits.

At the port, you board your private boat. You head to the Meeting of the Waters, where the black Rio Negro and the café-au-lait Solimões run side by side; your guide may let you dip your hand in each to feel the difference in temperature. You continue to Janauari lake, where a walkway leads through the forest to ponds of Victoria amazonica, the giant water lilies whose leaves can reach 2 metres across. A small canoe takes you through the igapó, the flooded forest, with sloths, monkeys and birds such as kingfishers and herons.

Lunch of grilled tambaqui and other river fish is at a floating restaurant. In the afternoon, you cross the Rio Negro to a spot where pink river dolphins, or botos, come close to the platform, and you can see them from the water's edge. You return to Manaus at about 16:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:15 – Teatro Amazonas.
09:15 – Adolpho Lisboa market.
10:00 – Boat to the Meeting of the Waters.
11:00 – Janauari lake and the water lilies.
12:00 – Canoe through the flooded forest.
13:00 – Lunch in a floating restaurant.
14:30 – Pink river dolphins.
16:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Bring insect repellent, a hat and sun cream.
• Visits to indigenous communities can be arranged respectfully with partner organisations.
• Swimming with dolphins is not offered, for their welfare.

INCLUDED: private car and boat, licensed guide, theatre entrance, canoe ride, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Will we see pink dolphins?
faq.answer: Very likely; they come close at the platform we visit. They are wild, so sightings are never guaranteed.

faq.question: Is the boat private?
faq.answer: Yes, a private motorboat with crew, plus a small canoe for the flooded forest.

faq.question: Is it safe to be on the river?
faq.answer: Yes. Life jackets are on board and the crews are experienced.

faq.question: Are there many mosquitoes?
faq.answer: Fewer than you might think on the Rio Negro, whose acidic water deters them; bring repellent anyway.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the dolphins and the water lilies. Child life jackets are provided.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Boarding the boats and canoes requires steps; the walkway to the water lilies is level.

faq.question: Can we stay in the jungle?
faq.answer: Yes. We arrange stays of 2 to 4 nights at jungle lodges on the Rio Negro.

faq.question: Do we need vaccinations?
faq.answer: Yellow fever vaccination is recommended for the Amazon; check with your doctor.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light, long-sleeved clothes, a hat, sun protection, insect repellent and sandals or light shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. High water (May to July) is best for canoeing in the flooded forest; low water (September to November) brings beaches.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Brazil but never required. If you were happy with your guide and driver, a small tip at the end of the day is a kind gesture.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
